Theme 003 · Product UI as the stage

Multiplayer Cursors

A shared design-tool canvas where the cast are named cursors: one human on call, and a teal cursor labelled Acme Pulse that quietly inspects every chart frame. When the camera switches to follow mode we literally watch the agent work, and the human flies over to make the call.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Named cursor + label pill — the characters: ink “Sam · on call” and teal “Acme Pulse”.
  • Selection box with handles — what a character is inspecting; snaps on beats.
  • Avatar stack — who is present; Pulse joining is the reveal.
  • Comment pin + thread — the anomaly and the human's options.
  • Cursor-chat bubble — short live remarks (“watching 14 metrics”).
  • Follow-mode frame — teal border + “Following Acme Pulse” = watching the agent work.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Interpolated cursor glide — bezier paths with 4–6 % overshoot, 0.6–0.9 s sine.inOut, never linear; arrival is quantised to the beat (every 1 s at 120 BPM).
  • Selection snap — box scales 1.06→1 in 0.18 s on a snare, handles pop 0.03 s later.
  • Follow-cam — the camera eases to the agent's viewport with a 0.2 s lag (power2.out 0.8 s) so the move feels like a person catching up; border draws on in 1 beat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: it makes the agent and the human visible as co-workers on one canvas; follow mode is a native, already-understood way to say “watch what the agent is doing”. Risk: more than 2–3 cursors reads as chaos, and tiny chart frames die at feed size, so zoom until one frame fills half the square.

Adapt to your product: swap the chart frames for your own screens or objects and name the agent cursor after your feature; the comment thread carries your product's single most important alert.
